what: The grand pipeline: scratch -> build -> deliver -> repair, and the routes through it.

stages.name: Scratch
stages.what: Take an idea, give it a spec, and stand up the repository with its guards already on.

stages.name: Build
stages.what: Prove the code, build every platform it ships on, and lint what was written.

stages.name: Deliver
stages.what: Publish the release, deploy the live demo, capture the screenshot, and give every app a landing page.

dispatchable.name: Add download blocks to landing pages

members.name: Add download blocks to landing pages

stages.name: Repair
stages.what: Find what broke, re-run what is transient, escalate what is not, audit the kits, learn from the record, and back up before any merge.
stages.input: none - it runs on a schedule

routes.name: A new app, from one sentence
then: the scaffold stands up the repo
app-deliver adds the landing page, the demo and the pipeline
build makes the EXE, the APK and the Linux binary
release publishes them, pages deploys the demo, shot captures it
routes.why: One input. Everything after it is already wired - the only step that needs a human is the idea.

routes.name: Change an app that exists
you: Push, or merge a pull request
routes.why: Zero inputs. The push IS the instruction, and the demo and the release can never disagree because they come from one commit.

routes.name: Repair and keep honest
then: self-diagnose reports what is broken or silently failing
backup snapshots every repo before a merge
routes.why: Zero inputs, and it is the stage that catches the failures nobody is watching.

routes.name: Ship a release on demand
you: Press Run workflow on the app's Build + deploy
routes.why: One press. For when you want a release now rather than on the next push.
